target.title: Add per-agent sandbox session visibility override feature
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: sandboxed session tools always applied the default sandbox session visibility clamp before considering the requesting agent, so `agents.list[].sandbox.sessionToolsVisibility` could be configured but was not consistently honored.
- Runtime impact: operators could not safely give one named sandboxed agent full configured session visibility while keeping other sandboxed agents clamped to spawned sessions.
- Change: session visibility resolution now derives the requester agent first, checks that agent's sandbox override, and falls back to `agents.defaults.sandbox.sessionToolsVisibility` only when no per-agent override exists.
- Compatibility: existing configs keep the same default `"spawned"` clamp unless a named agent explicitly sets `sandbox.sessionToolsVisibility`.

## User-Visible Behavior

New optional per-agent config:

```json
{
  "agents": {
    "defaults": {
      "sandbox": { "sessionToolsVisibility": "spawned" }
    },
    "list": [
      { "id": "tony", "sandbox": { "sessionToolsVisibility": "all" } }
    ]
  }
}
```

For sandboxed session tools, precedence is:

```text
agents.list[].sandbox.sessionToolsVisibility
agents.defaults.sandbox.sessionToolsVisibility
default spawned clamp
```

## Security Impact

- Data access scope can broaden only for an explicitly named sandboxed agent.
- The global/default sandbox behavior remains clamped to spawned sessions.
- Existing `tools.sessions.visibility` and `tools.agentToAgent` policy checks still apply; this does not bypass cross-agent policy.
- No secrets, credentials, network calls, shell execution, or gateway auth behavior changed.

## Files in This PR

- `CHANGELOG.md` - records the user-facing runtime/config behavior change.
- `docs/gateway/config-agents.md` - documents per-agent sandbox session visibility.
- `docs/gateway/config-tools.md` - documents session tool visibility and sandbox override precedence.
- `docs/tools/multi-agent-sandbox-tools.md` - documents multi-agent sandbox session tool behavior.
- `src/agents/openclaw-tools.ts` - wires requester identity into session tool construction.
- `src/agents/tools/session-status-tool.ts` - applies requester-aware sandbox visibility to `session_status`.
- `src/agents/tools/sessions-access.ts` - centralizes requester-aware sandbox visibility resolution.
- `src/agents/tools/sessions-helpers.ts` - forwards requester context through shared session helper wiring.
- `src/agents/tools/sessions-history-tool.ts` - applies requester-aware visibility to `sessions_history`.
- `src/agents/tools/sessions-list-tool.ts` - applies requester-aware visibility to `sessions_list`.
- `src/agents/tools/sessions-send-tool.ts` - applies requester-aware visibility to `sessions_send`.
- `src/agents/openclaw-tools.session-status.test.ts` - covers requester-aware `session_status` behavior.
- `src/agents/openclaw-tools.sessions-visibility.test.ts` - covers tool-factory wiring for the override.
- `src/agents/openclaw-tools.sessions.test.ts` - covers end-to-end session tool behavior through the OpenClaw tool factory.
- `src/agents/tools/sessions-access.test.ts` - covers access-layer override/fallback resolution.

## Verification

- `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD`
- `./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check src/agents/openclaw-tools.session-status.test.ts src/agents/openclaw-tools.sessions-visibility.test.ts src/agents/openclaw-tools.sessions.test.ts src/agents/openclaw-tools.ts src/agents/tools/session-status-tool.ts src/agents/tools/sessions-access.test.ts src/agents/tools/sessions-access.ts src/agents/tools/sessions-helpers.ts src/agents/tools/sessions-history-tool.ts src/agents/tools/sessions-list-tool.ts src/agents/tools/sessions-send-tool.ts`
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core.tsbuildinfo`
- `OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 OPENCLAW_VITEST_NO_OUTPUT_TIMEOUT_MS=360000 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/tools/sessions-access.test.ts src/agents/openclaw-tools.sessions-visibility.test.ts src/agents/openclaw-tools.sessions.test.ts src/agents/openclaw-tools.session-status.test.ts src/agents/tools/sessions.test.ts --reporter=dot`
  - Result: 10 test files passed, 268 tests passed.

## Real Behavior Proof

Behavior addressed: a sandboxed named agent with `agents.list[].sandbox.sessionToolsVisibility="all"` can use the configured `tools.sessions.visibility` scope, while sandboxed agents without that override remain clamped to spawned sessions.

Real environment tested: local OpenClaw checkout using production `createOpenClawTools`, embedded OpenClaw gateway session handlers, and real temporary `sessions.json` stores for `main` and `tony`.

Exact steps or command run after this patch: `node --import tsx --input-type=module -e <inline proof script>` from the repo root. The script created an isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, wrote real per-agent session stores, enabled embedded mode, constructed sandboxed `sessions_list` tools for `main` and `tony`, and compared observed session keys with expected visibility.

Evidence after fix:

```json
{
  "config": {
    "toolsSessionsVisibility": "all",
    "agentToAgent": { "enabled": true, "allow": ["*"] },
    "defaultSandboxSessionToolsVisibility": "spawned",
    "tonySandboxSessionToolsVisibility": "all"
  },
  "observed": {
    "mainSandboxedKeys": ["agent:main:subagent:main-child"],
    "tonySandboxedKeys": [
      "agent:main:main",
      "agent:main:subagent:main-child",
      "agent:tony:main",
      "agent:tony:subagent:tony-child"
    ]
  },
  "result": "PASS"
}
```

Observed result after fix: `main` stayed clamped to spawned sessions through the default sandbox setting; `tony` honored the per-agent `"all"` override and saw the full configured session scope when `tools.agentToAgent` allowed cross-agent access.

What was not tested: remote Crabbox/Testbox behavior. Crabbox is not installed in this shell, and the available Blacksmith CLI is unauthenticated.

## Risk and Rollback

- Risk: an operator may grant broad session visibility to the wrong named agent.
- Mitigation: the override is explicit per agent, default behavior is unchanged, and cross-agent policy remains enforced.
- Rollback: remove `agents.list[].sandbox.sessionToolsVisibility` from the agent entry to return to the default sandbox clamp.

target.title: feat(slack): add ignoreOtherMentions channel config
target.body:
## Summary

- Add `ignoreOtherMentions` option for Slack channel config, mirroring the existing Discord guild/channel feature
- When enabled, messages that mention another user (`<@U...>`) but do not explicitly mention the bot are dropped — even inside bot-participated threads
- This prevents the bot from replying when a user is talking to a coworker in a thread where the bot previously responded

## Slack vs Discord difference

Discord's `ignoreOtherMentions` checks `!wasMentioned && !implicitMention`. The Slack version intentionally omits the `!implicitMention` check because Slack's implicit mention (via `hasSlackThreadParticipation`) fires for **every** message in any bot-participated thread, which would make the feature ineffective.

## Config example

```json5
{
  channels: {
    slack: {
      channels: {
        "*": { ignoreOtherMentions: true },
      },
    },
  },
}
```

## Changed files

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/config/types.slack.ts` | Add `ignoreOtherMentions` to `SlackChannelConfig` |
| `src/config/zod-schema.providers-core.ts` | Add zod validation for the new field |

target.title: feat: add tools.fs.roots — per-agent filesystem roots with access modes
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: `tools.fs.workspaceOnly` is binary, so operators cannot safely allow agents to read or write a specific host path outside the workspace without opening broader filesystem access.
- Why it matters: multi-tenant and shared-gateway deployments often need narrowly scoped access to shared data, context files, or mounted knowledge directories.
- What changed: added `tools.fs.roots`, an explicit allowlist of filesystem roots with per-root `kind` (`dir`/`file`) and `access` (`ro`/`rw`), wired through host-mode FS tools, `apply_patch`, local media loading, outbound local-media/reply-delivery paths, and prompt-image auto-load.
- Host-mode `read` operations now use pinned file-descriptor root-scoped reads (`readFileWithinRoot`/`openFileWithinRoot`) to close the TOCTOU gap between path validation and file open, in addition to the existing pre-guard.
- Sandbox outbound media delivery now explicitly ignores configured `tools.fs.roots`, preventing sandbox-generated attachments from being rejected when host-mode roots are configured.
- What did NOT change: sandbox mode still relies on Docker isolation and ignores `tools.fs.roots`; `exec` sandboxing is unchanged; `tools.allow` / `tools.deny` behavior is unchanged.

## Change Type (select all)

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [x] Docs
- [x] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [x] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [x] Integrations
- [x] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #
- Related #
- [ ] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Root Cause / Regression History (if applicable)

- Root cause: existing FS policy exposed only two modes for host paths: workspace-only or unrestricted.
- Missing capability: there was no way to express "this agent may read `/data/shared/context.md` but may not read the rest of the host".
- Why now: this is needed for shared-gateway / multi-tenant deployments where the workspace boundary alone is too coarse.
- If unknown, what was ruled out: sandbox mode stays out of scope because sandbox tools resolve container paths, not host paths, and partial host-path enforcement there would create an inconsistent security model.

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

- Coverage level that should catch this:

  - [ ] End-to-end test

  - `extensions/googlechat/src/channel.test.ts`

- Scenarios locked in:
  - lexical dir/file root matching and ro/rw enforcement
  - canonical-root precedence over alias roots for host-mode mutation paths
  - unlink/delete behavior preserving symlink-entry semantics while still respecting stricter canonical roots

target.title: feat: expose rawBody on user messages in plugin hook events
target.body:
### Summary

Add `rawBody` field to user messages in `agent_end`, `before_prompt_build`, and `before_agent_start` (legacy) hook events. This provides plugins with the original user input before channel structural context, `buildInboundUserContextPrefix()` metadata, and prompt-build hook injections are prepended.

### Motivation

Plugin hooks receive `event.messages` where user message `content` includes OpenClaw-injected metadata (timestamps, channel info, sender IDs) and other hook injections (e.g., memory context). Plugins that process user content for purposes like memory extraction, summarization, or analytics must parse and strip this metadata — a fragile approach since the format varies by channel, chat type, and OpenClaw version.

PR #51502 already established the precedent of using `RawBody` instead of `Body` to avoid passing envelope metadata to LLM processing. This PR extends that principle to plugin hook events.

### Changes

- Compute `rawBodyForHooks` from `CommandBody ?? RawBody ?? Body` in the channel message handler — the clean user text without @mentions, sender labels, or message annotations
- Thread `rawBody` through the run params chain: `get-reply-run.ts` → `runReplyAgent` → `runAgentTurnWithFallback` → `runEmbeddedPiAgent` → `runEmbeddedAttempt`
- Include `rawBody` in hook event objects for `before_prompt_build`, `before_agent_start`, and `agent_end`
- Add `rawBody` to `FollowupRun` type so the value survives queueing/deferred runs
- `rawBody` is `undefined` for non-channel runs (CLI, heartbeat, cron)
- **Steer race fix** (`86ebda8b`): Thread `rawBody` through the steer queue path so steered injections on non-Telegram channels refresh the active embedded run's hook context

### Backward Compatibility

- Additive optional field only — no breaking changes
- Plugins can feature-detect `rawBody` and fall back to `content`:
  ```typescript
  const userText = event.rawBody ?? extractText(lastUser.content);
  ```
- Plugin SDK API baseline unchanged (no drift)

### Use Case

Memory plugins send user+assistant pairs to backend for memory extraction. Without `rawBody`, the plugin must regex-strip injected XML blocks and cannot remove inbound metadata, causing noisy "memories" from message IDs and timestamps. With `rawBody`, the plugin gets clean user input directly.

### Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: Plugin hook events (`before_prompt_build`, `agent_end`) now expose `event.rawBody` containing clean user-input text (22 chars) instead of requiring plugins to parse the metadata-decorated `messages[-1].content` (411 chars). Non-channel origins (heartbeat, cron, exec-event) correctly emit `rawBody: undefined`. Steered injections on non-Telegram channels now refresh `rawBody` via the steer queue path.

Real environment tested: Linux 6.17.0-1013-aws (arm64), Node v22.22.2, OpenClaw 2026.5.20, Bedrock `global.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7` (us-east-1, IAM role auth), Telegram bot `@oc_jmu_bot` via long-poll, custom probe plugin (`rawbody-probe`) using `definePluginEntry` + `api.on("before_prompt_build")` + `api.on("agent_end")`.

Exact steps or command run after this patch: Built from PR HEAD (`git rev-parse HEAD` = `29e89cfb84`), ran `pnpm build`, started gateway with `node openclaw.mjs gateway --allow-unconfigured --port 18799 --bind loopback --auth none --verbose`. Sent Telegram DM "hello rawbody test 004" to `@oc_jmu_bot`. Triggered heartbeat via `node openclaw.mjs system event --text "..." --mode now --url ws://127.0.0.1:18799 --token anonymous --json`. Ran unit tests: `pnpm exec vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-run.media-only.test.ts -t "rawBody hook gating" --reporter=verbose`.

Evidence after fix:
```
Case A — Channel happy path (Telegram DM):
[rawbody-probe] runId    = 4c1c5a9b-8e2c-405f-b6f3-d2246e4912cc
[rawbody-probe] trigger  = user
[rawbody-probe] rawBody  = "hello rawbody test 004"   (22 chars)
[rawbody-probe] lastUser = "Conversation info (untrusted metadata):\n...
                            hello rawbody test 003"   (411 chars)

Case B — Heartbeat origin:
[rawbody-probe] runId    = 40d31407-6882-4f23-bdc7-85ba18fb5a41

[rawbody-probe] rawBody  = <undefined>

Unit tests after fix (6/6 pass):
✓ passes user text as rawBody for telegram channel runs       (62ms)
✓ gates rawBody to undefined for heartbeat runs               (2ms)
✓ gates rawBody to undefined for cron-event runs              (1ms)
✓ gates rawBody to undefined for exec-event runs              (1ms)

The steer path unit test confirms `followupRun.rawBody` is threaded through for non-Telegram channels (discord provider).

Fixes #75658

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw sessions cleanup --dry-run` did not preview stale `.deleted.*` and `.reset.*` archive files, and the apply summary did not report when those physical archive files were removed. Operators could see only unreferenced-artifact counts even when deleted/reset session archives were the files consuming disk.

## Why This Change Was Made

The cleanup command already had an archive retention helper, but dry-run did not call it and store maintenance discarded its removal count. This change reuses the existing archive-retention rules for both preview and apply reporting instead of adding a second cleanup policy.

Reviewer follow-up: dry-run archive cleanup now accepts an exclusion set, and the sessions cleanup preview passes in the disk-budget simulated removal paths. A stale archive already claimed by disk-budget cleanup is therefore not counted again as deleted/reset archive cleanup.

target.title: fix(cron): stop fallback attempts when cron budget is exhausted
target.body:
## Problem

When a cron job's primary model times out near the cron deadline, the fallback model is started but immediately killed by the same cron timeout — receiving effectively 0ms to make an LLM request. The fallback never gets a fair chance to respond, and the user sees a misleading `cron: job execution timed out` error attributed to the fallback model.

**Observed in production logs (2026-03-22):**

```
[08:10:30.733] anthropic/claude-opus-4-6 attempt=1/2 reason=unknown err='Request was aborted.' duration=28667ms
[08:10:30.735] openai-codex/gpt-5.4    attempt=2/2 reason=timeout err='cron: job execution timed out' duration=0ms
```

The cron timeout wraps the entire fallback chain. When the primary model consumes most of the budget, the fallback model is allocated ~0ms and fails immediately.

## Solution

1. **Propagate the cron deadline** (`deadlineAtMs`) from `executeJobCoreWithTimeout` through the cron service state down to `runCronIsolatedAgentTurn`.

2. **Add a `beforeAttempt` hook** to `runWithModelFallback` that is called before each candidate attempt. If it returns `{ type: 'stop' }`, the fallback chain stops and preserves the original error from the previous attempt.

3. **Check remaining budget** in the cron layer's `beforeAttempt` callback. If less than `min(30s, timeout/4)` remains before the cron deadline, the fallback is skipped with a clear message:
   > `Skipping fallback: only 50ms remain before cron timeout (need at least 30000ms).`

This ensures:
- The primary model's real error is preserved (not masked by a fake cron timeout on the fallback)
- No wasted LLM API calls that would be aborted instantly
- The `beforeAttempt` hook is generic and reusable for other pre-attempt checks

## Changes

- `src/agents/model-fallback.ts` — Add `beforeAttempt` hook + `stop_before_candidate` decision type
- `src/cron/service/timer.ts` — Compute and pass `deadlineAtMs` to job execution
- `src/cron/isolated-agent/run.ts` — Use `beforeAttempt` to check remaining cron budget
- `src/cron/service/state.ts` + `src/gateway/server-cron.ts` — Thread `deadlineAtMs` through interfaces

## Tests

- `model-fallback.test.ts` — beforeAttempt stop behavior
- `run.fallback-time-budget.test.ts` — Cron deadline propagation + fallback budget exhaustion
- `service.issue-regressions.test.ts` — Deadline passed to isolated runs


## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed:** Cron isolated agent-turn jobs should not start a model fallback when the primary attempt has consumed almost the whole cron deadline and the fallback would be killed immediately by the same timeout.

**Real environment tested:** Local OpenClaw checkout on branch `fix/cron-fallback-timeout` at `008791fa10`, macOS host, Node 22. The proof command uses the same fallback budget formula added in this branch and the cron job shape from the affected isolated agent-turn surface.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Ran `node .artifacts/pr-52365-real-behavior-proof.mjs` locally after the patch, then ran `pnpm test src/cron/isolated-agent/run.fallback-time-budget.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose` as supplemental coverage for the same gate.

**Evidence after fix:** Terminal output from the local reproduction command:

```
$ node .artifacts/pr-52365-real-behavior-proof.mjs
cron fallback budget repro
job: sessionTarget=isolated wakeMode=next-heartbeat payload=agentTurn timeoutSeconds=60
primary attempt: consumed 59900ms of a 60000ms cron deadline
fallback check: remainingMs=100; fallbackMinRemainingMs=15000
before(upstream/main): runWithModelFallback had no beforeAttempt budget gate -> fallbackAttempted=true
after(this branch): fallbackAttempted=false
after stop: Skipping fallback: only 100ms remain before cron timeout (need at least 15000ms).
```

Supplemental targeted test output:

```
$ pnpm test src/cron/isolated-agent/run.fallback-time-budget.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose
✓ allows fallback attempts when the per-attempt budget fits inside the remaining cron deadline
✓ uses agents.defaults.timeoutSeconds for fallback budget when job timeoutSeconds is unset
✓ stops new fallback attempts when the per-attempt budget no longer fits
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests  3 passed (3)
```

**Observed result after fix:** With only 100ms left before the cron deadline and a 15,000ms minimum fallback budget, the after-fix gate returns `fallbackAttempted=false` and reports `Skipping fallback: only 100ms remain before cron timeout (need at least 15000ms).` The before behavior had no `beforeAttempt` budget gate, so the fallback candidate was started even though it could only receive about 0ms.

**What was not tested:** Live Anthropic/OpenAI API calls were not run for this proof; the local reproduction covers the cron fallback budget decision and the targeted test covers the runtime hook path with mocked provider execution.

target.title: feat: configurable default agent ID (escape the 'main' prison) 🦞
target.body:
## Summary

Adds support for overriding the hardcoded `"main"` fallback agent ID, so users with a single custom-named agent no longer get a ghost `agents/main/` default path/session identity when no `agents.list` is configured.

## The Problem

`DEFAULT_AGENT_ID` falls back to `"main"`. Some resolution paths run from partial config or before a full multi-agent list exists, so a setup that intends a custom default agent can still resolve the main session key and default agent directory as `main`.

## Solution

Two complementary override mechanisms:

### 1. Config key: `agents.defaultAgentId`

```json
{
  "agents": {
    "defaultAgentId": "maine-lobster"
  }
}
```

### 2. Env var: `OPENCLAW_DEFAULT_AGENT_ID`

```bash
export OPENCLAW_DEFAULT_AGENT_ID=maine-lobster
```

### Priority (highest → lowest)

1. `agents.list[].default: true` (explicit default agent)
2. `agents.list[0]` (first configured agent)
3. `agents.defaultAgentId` config key
4. `OPENCLAW_DEFAULT_AGENT_ID` env var
5. Hardcoded `"main"` (backward compatible)

## Changes

- Adds `agents.defaultAgentId` to the config schema/types and generated docs baseline.
- Updates `resolveDefaultAgentId()`, `listAgentIds()`, `resolveDefaultAgentDir()`, and main-session key resolution to honor config/env fallback values.
- Keeps populated `agents.list` behavior unchanged: list default/first entry still wins.
- Updates provider auth/default-agent directory resolution to use the effective default agent.
- Adds regression tests for config default, env fallback, default dir, and main-session key behavior.

## Testing

- `pnpm config:schema:check`
- `pnpm config:docs:check`
- `pnpm test src/agents/agent-scope-config.test.ts src/config/sessions/main-session.test.ts src/config/sessions/session-key.test.ts src/commands/auth-choice.test.ts src/commands/auth-choice.apply.plugin-provider.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`
- `pnpm check:changed`
- `git merge-tree --write-tree HEAD origin/main` → merge-clean

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: A config-only default agent ID should stop OpenClaw from falling back to the hardcoded `main` agent for the default agent directory and main session key.
- **Real environment tested**: Local OpenClaw checkout rebased onto latest `origin/main`, running the patched TypeScript source directly with Node/tsx in `/root/.openclaw/workspace/openclaw-pr-acpx/pr-51762`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

```console
$ node --import tsx --input-type=module <<'EOF'
import { resolveDefaultAgentId, resolveDefaultAgentDir } from './src/agents/agent-scope-config.ts';
import { resolveMainSessionKey } from './src/config/sessions/main-session.ts';
const cfg = { agents: { defaultAgentId: 'Ops Team' }, session: { mainKey: 'main' } };
const env = { OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR: '/tmp/openclaw-real-proof' };
console.log('defaultAgentId=' + resolveDefaultAgentId(cfg, env));
console.log('defaultAgentDir=' + resolveDefaultAgentDir(cfg, env));
console.log('mainSessionKey=' + resolveMainSessionKey(cfg, env));
EOF
```

- **Evidence after fix**: Terminal output copied from the patched real source command above:

```console
defaultAgentId=ops-team
defaultAgentDir=/tmp/openclaw-real-proof/agents/ops-team/agent
mainSessionKey=agent:ops-team:main
```

- **Observed result after fix**: `agents.defaultAgentId: "Ops Team"` is normalized to `ops-team`, the default agent directory resolves under `/tmp/openclaw-real-proof/agents/ops-team/agent`, and the main session key resolves to `agent:ops-team:main` instead of `main`.
- **What was not tested**: No browser/UI flow was tested; this PR changes config/session/agent resolution behavior and was verified through the live runtime resolver functions plus the targeted regression/check suite above.

Fixes #17477 🦞

target.title: fix: persist pending followup queues across gateway restart
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes #51620 — gateway restart drops queued and in-flight inbound messages.

## Changes

### New: `src/auto-reply/reply/queue/persist.ts`
Serializes all non-empty `FOLLOWUP_QUEUES` entries to `state/pending-messages.json` before shutdown. Strips non-portable fields (`config`, `skillsSnapshot`) and stores a version marker + timestamp.

### New: `src/gateway/server-pending-messages.ts`
On startup, reads the persisted file, injects missed messages as system events into their respective sessions (so the agent processes them on next turn), then deletes the file. Includes a 5-minute staleness guard to avoid replaying ancient messages from stale files.

### Modified: `src/gateway/server-close.ts`
Calls `persistFollowupQueues(FOLLOWUP_QUEUES)` before `chatRunState.clear()` so queue state is captured while still available. Best-effort — failure doesn't block shutdown.

### Modified: `src/gateway/server-startup.ts`
Calls `replayPersistedPendingMessages()` 1.5s after startup (after channels initialize), alongside the existing `scheduleRestartSentinelWake`.

## Tests

16 new tests covering:
- `persistFollowupQueues`: empty queues, non-empty queues, config stripping, multiple queues
- `consumePersistedQueues`: no file, read+delete, staleness guard (>5min), corrupt file, wrong version
- Round-trip: persist → consume
- `replayPersistedPendingMessages`: no entries, empty entries, system event injection, multiple queues, prompt truncation, empty items skip

## Limitations / Follow-up

This PR covers **Phase 1**: persisting in-memory followup queue items across restart.

Still not covered (follow-up work):
- **Phase 2**: Messages arriving during the drain window (hitting `GatewayDrainingError`) — these are rejected at the channel level before reaching the queue
- **Phase 3**: Channel-level message acknowledgment deferral — for channels that support it (Slack Socket Mode), defer ACK until message is processed or persisted so the platform can redeliver

## Testing

```
npx vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/queue/persist.test.ts src/gateway/server-pending-messages.test.ts
```

All 16 tests pass.

---

target.title: fix(skills): list omitted skill names when prompt is truncated
target.body:
## Problem

When many skills are installed (e.g. 45+), the prompt truncation at `maxSkillsPromptChars` (default 30KB) silently drops skills near the end of the alphabetically-sorted list. The agent sees only a generic `⚠️ Skills truncated: included N of M` message but has **no way to discover which skills were omitted** — it cannot use them even when directly relevant to the user's request.

Real-world example: a user sends a `mp.weixin.qq.com` link, but the `wechat-reader` skill (w-prefix, sorted last) is truncated out. The agent falls back to `curl`, which fails because WeChat articles are JS-rendered.

## Solution

When skills are truncated, the note now includes the **names** of omitted skills (capped at 1KB to stay compact) and suggests `openclaw skills info <name>` or `openclaw skills list` so the agent can still discover and read them on demand.

**Before:**
```
⚠️ Skills truncated: included 40 of 45. Run `openclaw skills check` to audit.
```

**After:**
```
⚠️ Skills truncated: included 40 of 45. Run `openclaw skills check` to audit. Additional installed skills not expanded here: verify-on-browser, wechat-reader, web-search-plus, wrangler, video-frames. If a listed skill name becomes relevant, inspect it with `openclaw skills info <name>` or `openclaw skills list` before deciding whether to read its SKILL.md.
```

## Changes

- `applySkillsPromptLimits()` now returns `omittedSkills` alongside the existing fields
- New `formatTruncatedSkillNames()` builds a compact name list (hard-capped at 1KB)
- New `buildSkillsTruncationNote()` assembles the enriched truncation message
- Two new test cases covering name listing for both char-based and count-based truncation

## Tests

All 34 existing + new tests pass (`npx vitest run src/agents/skills`).

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed: Skills prompt truncation should keep the emitted prompt within `maxSkillsPromptChars` and advertise omitted skill identifiers that `openclaw skills info <name>` can resolve exactly, including raw keys with characters such as `<` and backticks.

Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw checkout on Darwin arm64, Node v22.22.2, pnpm 10.33.2, branch `fix/skills-truncation-visibility`, current HEAD `db926508c4`.

target.title: AI-assisted: Gateway hook event routing respects target agent session
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: Hook completion and error system events were always enqueued to the default agent main session, even when the hook ran against another agent.
- Why it matters: In multi-agent setups this leaked hook summaries, including email-derived content, across agent boundaries.
- What changed: Hook system events now resolve the effective target agent and enqueue to that agent's main session; tests now assert `hooks`-targeted events stay out of the default session.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): Hook execution, delivery behavior, and wake-hook routing were not otherwise changed.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Docs

- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #24693
- Related #24016

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

Hook completion/error summaries now appear only in the target agent's main session instead of leaking into the default agent session.

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? (`No`)
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? (`No`)
- New/changed network calls? (`No`)
- Command/tool execution surface changed? (`No`)
- Data access scope changed? (`Yes`)
- If any `Yes`, explain risk + mitigation:
  This reduces data exposure by scoping hook-generated system events to the intended agent session. No broader data access was added.

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: macOS
- Runtime/container: Node 22 / pnpm workspace
- Model/provider: N/A
- Integration/channel (if any): Hook gateway endpoints
- Relevant config (redacted): multi-agent config with default `main` agent and `hooks` agent

### Steps

1. Configure hooks with a target `agentId` of `hooks`.
2. Trigger `/hooks/agent` with a non-delivered hook run.
3. Inspect queued system events for `agent:main:main` and `agent:hooks:main`.

### Expected

- The hook summary is queued only in the target agent's main session.

### Actual

- Before this change it was queued in the default agent's main session.

## Evidence

Attach at least one:

- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after
- [ ] Trace/log snippets
- [ ] Screenshot/recording
- [ ] Perf numbers (if relevant)

## Human Verification (required)

What you personally verified (not just CI), and how:

- Verified scenarios: explicit `agentId: "hooks"`, agent-scoped request `sessionKey`, allowed-agent enforcement, wake hooks still landing in the default main session.
- Edge cases checked: fallback to default agent for unknown target agent IDs.
- What you did **not** verify: live Gmail hook traffic against a real multi-agent deployment.

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? (`Yes`)
- Config/env changes? (`No`)
- Migration needed? (`No`)
- If yes, exact upgrade steps:

## Failure Recovery (if this breaks)

- How to disable/revert this change quickly: revert the two commits in this PR.
- Files/config to restore: `src/gateway/server/hooks.ts` and `src/gateway/server.hooks.test.ts`
- Known bad symptoms reviewers should watch for: hook summaries not appearing in the target agent session, or wake hooks no longer reaching the default main session.

## Risks and Mitigations

- Risk: Hook runs that infer the effective agent from session key could misroute if the session key parsing changes elsewhere.
  - Mitigation: regression coverage now checks both explicit-agent and agent-scoped session-key flows.

AI-assisted: yes. Fully tested locally for the targeted hook suite and validated with `pnpm build`.

target.title: fix(kill-tree): verify process group leader before using group kill to prevent gateway SIGTERM (#76259)
target.body:
## PR #94697 — Risk Closure Supplement > **Status: ClawSweeper P1/P2 items addressed** ### What changed since v1 (post ClawSweeper review) | Version | Change | Closes | | ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------- | | v1 (commit 9fd6116) | Initial leader-check + `detached:true` override | #76259 main case | | v2 (commit 3b261a9) | Propagate `detached:true` through 6 caller sites | ClawSweeper P1 — detached descendant cleanup | | v3 (commit cede936) | Propagate `detached:true` to agent-core NodeExecutionEnv | ClawSweeper P1 — full caller audit | | v4 (commit 7fb01ea) | (a) 4 new fail-safe tests for ps failure modes
(b) `/proc//stat` Linux fallback
(c) Source-level caller audit table | ClawSweeper P1 availability + P2 validation | --- ### ClawSweeper items — closed #### [P1] Compatibility — shared omitted-option Unix cleanup now depends on ps **Status: closed by /proc fallback + fail-safe tests.** The shared `killProcessTree(pid)` path (omitted `detached`) calls `isProcessGroupLeader(pid)`, which now has two layers: 1. **Primary**: `ps -p -o pgid=` (works on macOS, Linux, FreeBSD) 2. **Secondary** (Linux only): `/proc//stat` field 5 (pgid) — works on distroless / scratch / minimal Alpine where `ps` is absent 3. **Tertiary fail-safe**: both fail → returns `false` → single-pid kill (no group kill, no gateway SIGTERM) The fail-safe path is now covered by 4 new tests in `kill-tree.test.ts`: - ✅ on Unix falls back to single-pid kill when ps throws - ✅ on Unix falls back to single-pid kill when ps exits non-zero - ✅ on Unix falls back to single-pid kill when ps stdout is non-numeric - ✅ on Unix falls back to single-pid kill when ps stdout is empty Worst-case behavior on a Linux image without `ps` and without `/proc` (extremely rare — e.g. chroot without procfs): single-pid kill is used. This is **strictly safer than the pre-PR main**, which would have done `process.kill(-pid, ...)` unconditionally and SIGTERM'd the gateway. #### [P1] Availability — detached descendant cleanup after leader exit **Status: closed by v2 caller audit.** The P1 scenario (detached leader exits → `isProcessGroupLeader` returns false → descendants orphaned) is closed by **all 6 detached-spawn callers now explicitly passing `detached: true`** to `killProcessTree` / `signalProcessTree`. The `detached: true` short-circuits the leader check (`opts?.detached === true || ...`), preserving group kill unconditionally. #### Caller audit table (source-level proof) | Caller file | Spawn line | Spawn `detached` value | Cleanup call site | Passes `detached: true`? | | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ | ------------------------ | | `packages/agent-core/src/harness/env/nodejs.ts` (NodeExecutionEnv.exec) | L319, L321 | `process.platform !== "win32"` | L298 (abort), L339 (timeout) | ✅ | | `packages/agent-core/src/harness/env/nodejs.ts` (runCommand helper) | L152 | **not set** (attached) | L162 | ✅ correctly **omitted** | | `src/agents/mcp-stdio-transport.ts` | L63, L65 | `process.platform !== "win32"` | L130, L134 | ✅ | | `src/agents/agent-bundle-lsp-runtime.ts` | L83, L87 | `process.platform !== "win32"` | L246 | ✅ | | `src/agents/shell-snapshot.ts` | L445, L447 | `process.platform !== "win32"` | L460, L464 | ✅ | | `src/agents/sessions/tools/bash.ts` | L63, L65 | `process.platform !== "win32"` | L77, L87 | ✅ | | `src/process/exec.ts` (runCommandWithTimeout) | L396, L402 | `killProcessTree && process.platform !== "win32"` (conditional) | L501 (inside `if (killProcessTree)` guard) | ✅ | **Invariant**: every caller that spawns with `detached: true` passes `detached: true` to cleanup; every caller that spawns attached passes nothing (or `detached: false`). The two cannot drift because they share the same `killProcessTree` option flag at the spawn site. #### [P2] Persistent data-model change detected in `src/agents/sessions/tools/bash.ts` **Status: false positive — no serialized state change.** The only change to `bash.ts` is on L77 and L87, where the existing `killProcessTree(child.pid)` call gains a second argument `{ detached: true }`. This is a function-call argument change, not a structural change to any persisted type. No `SessionState`, `BashSnapshot`, or serialized payload is touched. The `KillProcessTreeOptions` type itself was already extended with `detached?: boolean` in PR #71681; this PR only consumes the existing field. #### [P2] Run current-head process cleanup validation before merge **Status: closed by validation script.** Ran the exact [P1] acceptance criteria commands from ClawSweeper's review: ```bash # 1. kill-tree unit tests node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/process/kill-tree.test.ts # 2. agent cleanup paths node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/mcp-stdio-transport.test.ts \ src/agents/agent-bundle-lsp-runtime.test.ts # 3. exec / shell / bash node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/shell-snapshot.test.ts \ src/process/exec.test.ts ``` Real process-group behavior verified on macOS arm64 (Sequoia): - **Step A**: attached child → `isProcessGroupLeader? false` → single-pid kill used (expected) - **Step B**: detached child → `isProcessGroupLeader? true` → group kill reaches descendants (expected) --- ### Merge readiness - ✅ All ClawSweeper P1 items closed with source-level evidence - ✅ All ClawSweeper P2 items closed (false positive explained + validation run) - ✅ Test count: 19/19 (15 original + 4 fail-safe = 19) - ✅ No API change to `KillProcessTreeOptions` (existing `detached?: boolean` field) - ✅ No new runtime dependency (only `node:fs` for /proc fallback) - ✅ Backwards compatible: pre-PR main callers that omit `detached` see safer behavior (no gateway SIGTERM risk); callers that spawn detached and pass `detached: true` see identical behavior to pre-#71681 main - ✅ Windows path untouched --- **Ready for maintainer review.** --- ## Summary What problem does this PR solve? - `killProcessTree` on Unix defaults `useGroupKill` to `true` when callers omit `{ detached: false }`. If the PID is not its own process group leader, `process.kill(-pid, ...)` targets whatever process group `pid` belongs to — typically the gateway's own process group, causing the gateway to receive SIGTERM. Why does this matter now? - #71681 made the fix opt-in (callers must pass `{ detached: false }`), but any caller that omits the option still triggers the bug. On macOS with launchd-managed gateway, a non-detached child that becomes a zombie triggers `killProcessTree` → `process.kill(-pid, SIGTERM)` → gateway receives SIGTERM and exits. What is the intended outcome? - `killProcessTree` verifies whether the PID is its own process group leader via `ps -p -o pgid=` before using group kill. Non-leader PIDs fall back to single-pid kill, preventing accidental gateway signaling. - When the caller explicitly passes `detached: true`, group kill is used unconditionally (bypassing the leader check), preserving the ability to clean up detached process groups even after the group leader has exited. What is intentionally out of scope? - Windows behavior is unchanged (taskkill /T already handles tree termination correctly). The `detached: false` option is preserved as an explicit caller override. What does success look like? - All 15 vitest tests pass (10 original + 3 original new + 2 new for detached:true override). A non-group-leader PID receives single-pid kill while a group leader PID still receives group kill. A detached:true call forces group kill even after leader exit. What should reviewers focus on? - Whether `isProcessGroupLeader` using `spawnSync("ps", ...)` is acceptable for the kill path (it's not a hot path), and whether the 500ms timeout is appropriate. - The `detached:true` override added for the P1 fix in #94697 review. ## Linked context Which issue does this close? Closes #76259 Which issues, PRs, or discussions are related? - Related #71662 (original issue) - Related #71681 (original opt-in fix) - ClawSweeper review #94697 (P1: preserve detached group cleanup after leader exit) Was this requested by a maintainer or owner? Reporter issue with numbered repro and suggested fix; ClawSweeper queueable-fix criteria in comments. ## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs) **Behavior or issue addressed:** `killProcessTree` group-kill defaults to `true` and can SIGTERM the gateway when the PID is not a process group leader. After leader exit, `isProcessGroupLeader` returns false, but `detached:true` forces group kill. **Real environment tested:** local checkout on macOS arm64 (Sequoia), branch `fix/76259-kill-tree-group-leader`

## What Problem This Solves

Plugins need a portable way to add presentation buttons to outbound replies before channel rendering, without expanding the broad `message_sending` hook into a transport/presentation mutation API.

## Why This Change Was Made

This keeps `message_sending` focused on the logical outbound message contract and uses the existing `reply_payload_sending` boundary for presentation-level mutation. Buttons live on `ReplyPayload.presentation`, and `reply_payload_sending` runs after reply payload normalization but before channel rendering, which makes it the right place for portable button decoration.

OCA compared the earlier `message_sending` direction against this implementation and agreed the current `reply_payload_sending` approach is cleaner: it avoids adding payload shape, outbound metadata, precedence rules, and cross-channel rendering promises to the public `message_sending` API.

## User Impact

target.title: [codex] fix(sessions): report archive cleanup in sessions cleanup
target.body:
Fixes #75658

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw sessions cleanup --dry-run` did not preview stale `.deleted.*` and `.reset.*` archive files, and the apply summary did not report when those physical archive files were removed. Operators could see only unreferenced-artifact counts even when deleted/reset session archives were the files consuming disk.

## Why This Change Was Made

The cleanup command already had an archive retention helper, but dry-run did not call it and store maintenance discarded its removal count. This change reuses the existing archive-retention rules for both preview and apply reporting instead of adding a second cleanup policy.

Reviewer follow-up: dry-run archive cleanup now accepts an exclusion set, and the sessions cleanup preview passes in the disk-budget simulated removal paths. A stale archive already claimed by disk-budget cleanup is therefore not counted again as deleted/reset archive cleanup.

## User Impact

Users running `sessions cleanup` now see deleted/reset archive cleanup in dry-run output and in apply output. Forced cleanup also scans the store directory for stale deleted archives even when no session rows were removed, while `resetArchiveRetention: false` still preserves reset archives.

## Summary

- Why it matters: that made it possible for non-built-in tool results to be treated as trusted local media sources.
- What changed: local media passthrough now requires an exact raw-name match against the built-in tools registered for the run, client-tool name conflicts are rejected before execution, and plugin-origin metadata is preserved through tool wrappers.

target.title: feat(attach): record + resume the Claude cli session bound to an attach session
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

PR #96454 launches Claude Code bound to a gateway session, but the conversation is invisible to OpenClaw and lost on exit: the gateway never learns *which* Claude cli session the attach started, so it can't surface the transcript or let you continue the same conversation on the next attach.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is the **resume + recording** piece of the `attach` surface (tracking: openclaw/openclaw#96205, PR4). `openclaw attach` now starts Claude with a **known** session id (`claude --session-id <uuid>`) and **adopts** it into the gateway session — persisting the `{sessionKey ↔ cliSessionId}` binding. That binding does double duty:
- **Recording** — the gateway's existing history-import path (`resolveClaudeCliBindingSessionId` → `readClaudeCliSessionMessages` → `augmentChatHistoryWithCliSessionImports`) surfaces the attach conversation in `chat.history`. It was never wired to attach because nothing told the gateway the session id.
- **Resume** — the next attach to the same gateway session **and same cwd** resumes it (`claude --resume <id>`). Claude scopes sessions per project, so the binding records a `cwdHash` (`hashCliSessionText`) and `attach.grant` returns `resumeSessionId` only on a cwd match — mirroring the cli-backend's existing cwd-invalidation (`cli-session.ts`). A different cwd starts fresh (a different project is a different conversation), so a stale/foreign session never fails `claude --resume`.

It reuses existing storage end-to-end — `setCliSessionBinding` (with `cwdHash`) + the atomic `patchSessionEntry` write (which preserves other providers' bindings + creates the row if missing). **No** new tables, no `session-sync`/`meta.json`, no `conversations_list`.

## User Impact

- `openclaw attach` starts Claude with a known `--session-id` and binds it; re-attaching to the same session **resumes** the same conversation (`--resume`).
- The attach conversation is **recorded** (surfaced in gateway chat history) via the existing import path.
- New gateway method **`attach.adopt({ token, cliSessionId })`** (`operator.admin`); **`attach.grant` now also returns `resumeSessionId`**. Both additive to the (unreleased) attach surface; no protocol bump.
- **No change** to the cli-backend path or existing commands. Adopt is best-effort — a failed adopt never blocks the launch.

## Evidence

- **Gateway tests (16)**: grant/revoke/ttl + `resumeSessionId` returned **only on cwd match** + `attach.adopt` persists the `claude-cli` binding (with `cwdHash`) **preserving other providers' bindings** + `persisted` flag + adopt validation (missing field / unknown grant → `INVALID_REQUEST`).
- **CLI tests (15)**: adopt fires only on the child `"spawn"` event (not before launch, not on spawn-failure, not in `--print-config`), the `--resume` path, malformed-grant/expiry handling, and the spawn/revoke + signal-detach lifecycle.
- Build, oxlint, **import-cycles** all clean; the 276-test gateway suite + the advertised-method-list test pass with `attach.adopt` added.
- **Stack** (each gated on exit code): PR4 delta is 6 files on top of PR2; full stack vs main is 13 files. Stacked on #96454 (PR2) / #96351 (PR1).
- Mutation **68%**; autoreview clean (cwd-encoding + cwd-orphan findings fixed).
- **adopt-on-spawn**: `attach.adopt` fires only in the child `"spawn"` handler — once `claude` actually starts — so it never binds a session id that a `--print-config` (no launch) or a failed spawn would leave uncreated.
- **Real-behavior proof — real Claude Code 2.1.191 in an isolated container** (apple-container, no Docker). A real headless gateway auto-pairs the device as operator, so `attach.grant`/`attach.adopt` execute for real. Same gateway session key `agent:main:realclaude`; only the cwd changes. Tokens/device id redacted.

  **1) First attach, cwd `/work/alpha`** — attach spawns real `claude --session-id <A>`; claude runs and writes a genuine transcript; adopt fires ON SPAWN:
  ```text
  Attaching Claude Code to session agent:main:realclaude …
  Hello from Claude — acknowledged, the attached harness is working.        ← real claude's reply
  ~/.claude/projects/-work-alpha/9b748344-….jsonl  (10,939 bytes)
  entry types: {"user":1,"assistant":1,"queue-operation":2,"attachment":3,"ai-title":1,"last-prompt":1}   ← genuine Claude Code transcript
  ```
  **2) `chat.history` for the session** — OpenClaw imports the REAL transcript after adoption:
  ```text
  $ openclaw gateway call chat.history --params '{"sessionKey":"agent:main:realclaude"}'
  imported roles: 1 user + 1 assistant
  … "content": "hello from a real attached harness …"     ← the real prompt, imported
  ```
  **3) Re-attach, cwd `/work/alpha`** (same project) → resumes the SAME real session:
  ```text
  "launch": [ "claude", "--resume", "9b748344-…", "--mcp-config", "…" ]
  ```
  **4) Attach, cwd `/work/beta`** (different project) → fresh id, never `9b748344` (the cwd gate):
  ```text
  "launch": [ "claude", "--session-id", "32350be6-…", "--mcp-config", "…" ]
  ```
- `claude --resume <uuid>` parses the UUID **as the session id** (verified: `claude --resume <missing>` → "No conversation found with session ID: …"), so the `["--resume", id]` arg form is correct.

**Risks → mitigations:** adopt is best-effort (failed adopt never blocks launch); the binding is grant-scoped (`token → sessionKey`, never header-trusted); resume is cwd-scoped (`cwdHash` gate) so a foreign/stale session never fails the launch; the binding write is atomic (`patchSessionEntry`) so concurrent provider bindings aren't lost.

target.title: Preserve Codex output after missing turn completion
target.body:
## Summary

Supersedes the patch from #99167 because the original contributor branch cannot be pushed to by `100yenadmin` despite `maintainerCanModify=true`.

- Preserve captured assistant text only for Codex app-server `turn_completion_idle_timeout` failures from the completion-watch path.
- Fail closed when recovery could duplicate or replace side effects, terminal output, active Codex items, replay evidence, tool activity, cron writes, committed message sends, accepted session spawns, or async tool activity.
- Keep non-completion turn-watch timeouts, including progress-watch timeouts with assistant output, on the existing timeout/error path.
- Add deterministic embedded-runner regressions for safe assistant-output preservation, non-completion watchdogs, active item lifecycle, and terminal-state recovery blocking.
- Update the Codex harness docs so the recovery contract names terminal-output evidence as a recovery blocker.

## What Problem This Solves

Codex app-server can do useful work and produce assistant output but then fail to emit the terminal `turn/completed` event. OpenClaw needs a narrow mitigation for the safe completion-timeout case so the user does not lose a final answer, while still failing closed for non-completion watchdogs and side-effectful or terminal-output turns.

The prior #99167 draft allowed assistant-output recovery whenever `shouldSurfaceCodexCompletionTimeout` was true. That predicate is broader than completion-watch timeouts, so a progress-watch timeout with assistant text could be delivered as a successful reply. The first replacement patch narrowed delivery to `turnWatchTimeoutKind === "completion"` and required `itemLifecycle.activeCount === 0`. This revision also reuses `hasAttemptTerminalState(attempt)` so heartbeat responses, tool media, source replies, accepted spawns, async tools, cron writes, and committed messaging delivery evidence cannot be overwritten by recovered assistant text.

## Evidence

Refs #87744 and #88312. Related historical items: #78756, #84076, #82080, #89974, and openai/codex#22144.

Fresh local evidence from `2026-07-03` shows the target failure class separately from the later subscription/usage-limit failure:

- `2026-07-03 01:45 GMT+7`: `codex app-server turn idle timed out waiting for completion`, `failureKind=turn_completion_idle_timeout`, `turnWatchTimeoutKind=completion`, `lastActivityReason=turn:start`, `activeAppServerTurnRequests=0`, `activeTurnItemCount=0`, `terminalTurnNotificationQueued=false`.
- `2026-07-03 02:24 GMT+7`: separate `rate_limit` / subscription usage-limit failure. This PR does not address that second failure.

Red/green proof for the replacement patch and review fixes:

- RED on PR #99167 head before the code fix:
  - `OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 pnpm exec vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.agents-embedded-agent.config.ts --maxWorkers=1 --no-file-parallelism src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.codex-app-server-recovery.test.ts`
  - Failed: `does not deliver assistant output from non-completion Codex turn watch timeouts` received the assistant text as a successful payload.
- GREEN after the non-completion guard:
  - same embedded-runner command: `1 passed`, `12 passed`.
- RED for the ClawSweeper active-item review on PR head `c53227734a6337507d4f538e049a7523e04e2ebf`:
  - same embedded-runner command after adding `does not deliver assistant output while Codex item lifecycle is active`
  - Failed: expected the missing-completion error, but received `This active-item answer must stay withheld.` as a successful payload.
- GREEN after the active-item guard:
  - same embedded-runner command: `1 passed`, `13 passed`.
- RED for the ClawSweeper terminal-state review on PR head `e82b799baf5a9d6360b269218c75c3f68dc7767a`:
  - same embedded-runner command after adding terminal-state cases.
  - Failed: terminal heartbeat responses, tool media, tool media block replies, and source reply payloads still received recovered assistant output.
- GREEN after the terminal-state guard and lint cleanup on current head `f17142b86912eb7cb8da5f6c172e813e35484783`:
  - same embedded-runner command: `1 passed`, `21 passed`.
  - App-server event-stream proof: `node scripts/test-projects.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.turn-watches.test.ts -- --maxWorkers=1 --no-file-parallelism --reporter=dot`: `1 passed`, `66 passed`.

target.title: fix: system events render twice per turn when hooks add prompt context
target.body:
Closes #95323

> This PR is AI-assisted: the analysis, patch, and test were written with an AI coding agent. A human operator reviewed the change; the report's payload evidence came from a live deployment.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the one drained inbound system event is rendered twice in a single turn's model payload: once standalone before the raw user message and once inside the hidden "OpenClaw runtime context ..." message. On current main this happens whenever a `before_prompt_build` hook contributes prepend/append context (memory-injection plugins do this on essentially every turn), on any channel that enqueues inbound system events (Slack in the original report; Telegram shows zero because it enqueues none). The duplicated block is per-turn prompt noise the model has to read twice.

## Why This Change Was Made

The reply pipeline prepends drained system events into the model-visible bodies while keeping the transcript body clean, and `resolveRuntimeContextPromptParts` derives that same block as hidden runtime context. The plain path already renders once because the visible prompt falls back to the transcript text. The hook path threads a separate model prompt that still embeds the event block, producing the double render. The fix strips the derived hidden-context remainder back out of the visible model prompt at the split, restoring the invariant that the model-visible prompt never repeats the hidden runtime context. When the remainder is not a literal substring of the model prompt (inline-marker prompts), the model prompt is left untouched, so existing marker semantics are preserved.

## User Impact

Turns with pending system events (model switches, queue notices, and similar) and prompt-building hooks now deliver the event block once, via the runtime-context message, instead of twice. Transcript persistence and user-visible text are unchanged; channels without inbound system events are unaffected.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.unit-fast.config.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/runtime-context-prompt.test.ts` passes 18/18, including a new regression test: a hook-supplied model prompt embedding the drained event block comes back without it while the block remains in `runtimeContext`.
- Red/green: with the source change stashed, exactly the new test fails (17/18); restoring the change returns 18/18. The existing inline-marker tests ("keeps prompt-local additions in the model prompt", "keeps hidden runtime context separate from prompt-local additions") pass unchanged, covering the not-a-substring fallback.
- Mechanism chain on current main: events drained and prepended in `src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-run.ts` (drained blocks into `systemEventBlocks`) and `src/auto-reply/reply/prompt-prelude.ts` (prepended into `prefixedCommandBody`/`queuedBody`, not the transcript body); hook context makes `attempt.ts` pass a distinct `modelPrompt` into the split, which then returns both the event-bearing model prompt and the same block as `runtimeContext`, rendered again via `buildRuntimeContextCustomMessage`.
- Live payloads motivating the report showed the same drained event with the same timestamp both standalone before the raw message and inside the runtime-context wrapper (details in #95323).
- Full `pnpm build` / `pnpm check` deferred to CI (memory-constrained local host).

## What Problem This Solves Organizations on a data-residency GitHub Enterprise tenant (a `*.ghe.com` host such as `your-org.ghe.com`) could not use GitHub Copilot with OpenClaw. Copilot auth, token refresh, and completions were hardwired to public `github.com` / `api.github.com`, so onboarding via `openclaw models auth` and the Copilot provider offered no way to reach a tenant-local Copilot endpoint. Enterprise users were effectively locked out of the Copilot provider. ## Why This Change Was Made Adds GitHub Enterprise (data residency) as a first-class Copilot auth choice, nested alongside the existing GitHub and Local Proxy options. Picking it prompts for the tenant domain, runs the device login against that host, and persists the domain to `models.providers.github-copilot.params.githubDomain` so later token refreshes and completions resolve automatically. Domain resolution follows `COPILOT_GITHUB_DOMAIN` env > config > `github.com`. The domain is threaded through every Copilot code path — device flow, token exchange, completions, embeddings, image understanding, and simple-completion — so all features work on the tenant, not just chat. Public `github.com` behavior is unchanged (no config is written for the default host). No config schema change (uses free-form provider params). **Security (fail-closed by design):** the host allowlist is locked to `github.com` and `*.ghe.com` tenants only — any other value (typo or injected `COPILOT_GITHUB_DOMAIN`/config) falls back to `github.com` so the GitHub OAuth token can never be redirected to an arbitrary `api.`. The cached Copilot API token is scoped by the GitHub host it was minted for, so a public token is never reused against a tenant host (or vice versa) after a domain switch. ## User Impact Enterprise users can now authenticate Copilot against their `*.ghe.com` tenant directly from onboarding or `openclaw models auth` by choosing **GitHub Copilot (Enterprise / data residency)** and entering their domain — no manual URL editing. Chat, embeddings (memory search), and image understanding all route to the tenant. `COPILOT_GITHUB_DOMAIN` enables fully headless/CI setups. Non-enterprise users see no change. ## Evidence Live validation against a real data-residency GHE tenant (domain/token redacted): ### [P1] GHE Login, Token Refresh & Completion — Redacted Evidence 1. GHE Login / Auth pre-warm (gateway startup, 18:56:23 UTC) ``` subsystem=gateway level=INFO time=2026-07-02T18:56:23.756Z provider auth state pre-warmed in 477ms eventLoopMax=11.9ms ``` Stored GHE credential loaded and validated successfully on gateway boot. 2. Active GHE Copilot token state ``` integrationId: vscode-chat token: [REDACTED] updatedAt: 2026-07-02T21:03:31Z ← refreshed ~12 minutes ago expiresAt: 2026-07-02T21:33:31Z ← valid for ~17 more minutes expired? false ``` Standard 30-minute Copilot token TTL confirmed; token was refreshed mid-session against REDACTED.ghe.com. 3. Completion calls against GHE endpoint (sample) ``` subsystem=provider-transport-fetch level=INFO time=2026-07-02T21:09:19Z [model-fetch] start provider=github-copilot api=anthropic-messages model=claude-sonnet-4.6 method=POST url=https://copilot-api.REDACTED.ghe.com/v1/messages status=— [model-fetch] response provider=github-copilot api=anthropic-messages model=claude-sonnet-4.6 status=200 elapsedMs=1529 contentType=text/event-stream ``` Dozens of successful round-trips throughout the session (18:56 → 21:15 UTC), all status=200.

target.title: fix: first visible turn after reset waits out the stuck-session abort window
target.body:
Closes #99082

> This PR is AI-assisted: the analysis, patch, and tests were written with an AI coding agent. A human operator reviewed the change and traced the incident on a live deployment.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the first visible turn after a session reset waits out the full stuck-session abort window (default 360s) before it can be delivered. A committed reset rotates the store entry's sessionId, but the visible-reply registry is keyed by the stable session key, so a leftover operation registered under the archived sessionId keeps the reply slot latched. In multi-agent rooms this reliably wedges every agent except the first one to finish resetting: their "Session reset." acknowledgements and all queued inbounds wait ~6 minutes for the stuck-session recovery one-shot, and with stuck-session recovery disabled the wait is unbounded. Full traced incident (two rooms, ack latencies 9m48s and 11m46s, recovery reclaiming the stale work at exactly the abort threshold) is in #99082.

## Why This Change Was Made

Before visible dispatch admission, the dispatcher now force-clears an active reply operation that is provably superseded by a committed rotation. The guards, in order: terminal-recovery operations keep their existing protection; both the dispatch-start store snapshot AND a fresh store lookup must disagree with the operation's sessionId, so a mid-run rotation that has committed the store but not yet relabeled its own operation is never treated as stale; and terminal-status snapshots are excluded entirely, because terminal-session recovery admits a fresh operation with a new sessionId before the store entry rotates (#86827) and an id comparison alone cannot distinguish that from a leftover. The existing terminal-session force-clear block is untouched and continues to own the terminal case. Boundary: a turn that is already blocked inside the admission wait when the rotation commits still waits its configured timeout; every subsequent visible turn clears the leftover immediately, which removes the user-visible wedge.

## User Impact

/reset in a multi-agent room now acknowledges promptly on every agent instead of wedging all but one for ~6 minutes, and queued messages behind the reset no longer pile up. Deployments with stuck-session recovery disabled gain a bound they previously lacked. No configuration change; single-agent resets, terminal-session recovery, and normal busy handling behave exactly as before.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.auto-reply-reply.config.ts src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.stale-recovery.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/reply-run-registry.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/reply-turn-admission.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/session-reset-cleanup.test.ts` passes 275/275, including 2 new tests (a leftover operation from a rotated session is cleared without invoking stuck-session recovery; an active operation whose sessionId matches the store entry is never touched) and the existing terminal-snapshot invariant test "does not force-clear an active operation whose session id differs from the terminal snapshot", which caught an over-broad first revision of this check in CI and now passes with the terminal-snapshot exclusion.
- Red proof: with the source change stashed, the new rotated-session test does not merely fail, it hangs in the visible-admission wait until the test runner's no-output watchdog kills the process group, reproducing the reported wedge in miniature; with the change applied it completes immediately.
- Live incident motivating the fix: on a 2026.6.10 multi-agent gateway, /reset in two rooms wedged one agent per room for 9m48s and 11m46s with `stalled session ... recovery=none` warnings every 30s and `stuck session recovery reclaiming stale active reply work` firing at exactly the 360s threshold under the archived session id (logs and timeline in #99082).
- Full `pnpm build` / `pnpm check` deferred to CI (memory-constrained local host).

## What Problem This Solves

Bot Framework personal-chat attachment downloads call `/v3/attachments/{id}` and previously parsed the metadata with unbounded `response.json()`. A hostile or misbehaving endpoint could stream an arbitrarily large JSON body and OOM the gateway process before the attachment view download even starts.

Related open bounded-read work covers MS Teams Graph collection (#98833), Graph upload (#97784), and SSO (#97781), but not the Bot Framework `attachmentInfo` path in `bot-framework.ts`.

Note: Inworld TTS/voices bounded reads are already on `main` (#95416, #98660), so this PR targets the remaining MS Teams gap instead.

## Why This Change Was Made

Route the Bot Framework attachment metadata success path through the shared `readProviderJsonResponse` helper (16 MiB cap, stream cancel on overflow), matching sibling MS Teams Graph/OAuth bounded JSON reads.

## User Impact

No config or API changes. Personal DM / Bot Framework attachment downloads fail closed with a logged warning when attachment metadata JSON exceeds the cap, instead of buffering the full body.

## Evidence

Local proof (worktree `d:\WorkSpace\AI\openclaw-wt-inworld-bound-reads`, branch `fix/msteams-bound-bot-framework-attachmentinfo-json-reads`, commit `30054fe6d6`):

```bash

target.title: fix #98107: Gateway regenerates service-env file on every restart, wiping Telegram bot tokens
target.body:
Closes #98107

## Summary

- Preserve existing generated macOS LaunchAgent env-file values for config SecretRef environment keys when the install plan regenerates the gateway service environment.
- Track current config SecretRef env ids as managed service keys even when the current shell no longer contains the secret value.
- Keep fresh `.env` and current shell SecretRef values ahead of older generated env-file values.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running the gateway as a macOS LaunchAgent could lose Telegram bot token environment values after gateway service regeneration, causing Telegram startup to fail with invalid-token API errors after restart or update flows.

## Why This Change Was Made

The install-plan builder already receives parsed existing LaunchAgent env-file values and source provenance, but the managed render policy did not restore file-backed SecretRef values after deleting managed keys during regeneration. This change treats env ids referenced by current config SecretRefs as service-managed keys and restores only file-backed existing values for macOS LaunchAgent rendering when no fresher `.env` or shell SecretRef value is available.

## User Impact

Users who keep Telegram bot tokens in the generated LaunchAgent service env file no longer have those values replaced or dropped by placeholder config values during service-env regeneration. OpenClaw still avoids rendering ordinary config env values into the LaunchAgent env file, and stale inline service env values remain excluded.

## Root Cause

- **Root cause:** The LaunchAgent reader can parse `~/.openclaw/service-env/<label>.env` and mark entries as `file`, but `buildGatewayInstallPlan` only preserved non-managed existing env vars. During regeneration, `writeManagedServiceEnvKeysToEnvironment` removed managed keys and the render policy only re-added state-dir `.env` or current shell SecretRef values, so an existing generated env-file Telegram token was lost when the current shell did not contain it.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** The fix restores existing values specifically from `file` / `inline-and-file` provenance for keys still referenced by current config SecretRefs, then lets state-dir `.env` and current shell SecretRef values override them. That addresses the regeneration source of truth without making ordinary inline service env or unrelated stale keys durable.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Gateway install-plan regeneration for a macOS LaunchAgent with an existing generated env-file Telegram SecretRef token and config placeholder value.
- **Real environment tested:** Linux source checkout invoking the actual production `buildGatewayInstallPlan` code path with `platform: "darwin"`, an executable wrapper, existing env-file source metadata, and current Telegram SecretRef config. No mocked planner was used in this proof command.

target.title: fix: deleting a session leaves its trajectory artifacts orphaned on disk
target.body:
Closes #89200

> This PR is AI-assisted: the analysis, patch, and tests were written with an AI coding agent. A human operator reviewed the change and validated it against a live deployment's session store.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where deleting a session (dashboard delete or the `sessions.delete` RPC) leaves its trajectory artifacts orphaned on disk forever. The delete lifecycle archives the transcript but never touches the paired `.trajectory.jsonl` / `.trajectory-path.json` files, and the age-based maintenance path only cleans trajectories for entries it removes itself, so orphans accumulate until the blunt disk-budget sweep (which can also evict live sessions) happens to reclaim them.

## Why This Change Was Made

`deleteSessionEntryLifecycle` now removes the deleted session's trajectory artifacts inside the same exclusive store write, reusing the existing `removeRemovedSessionTrajectoryArtifacts` maintenance helper with the same safeguards as the age-prune path: a referenced-session guard (artifacts are kept while any other store entry still references the session id) and `restrictToStoreDir`. The cleanup is gated on `archiveTranscript`, so a `deleteTranscript: false` delete keeps the trajectory pair together with the preserved transcript.

## User Impact

Deleting a session from the dashboard or via RPC no longer leaks trajectory files into the sessions directory. No configuration change; deletes that keep the transcript keep the trajectory files too, and sessions still referenced by another store entry are untouched.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.runtime-config.config.ts src/config/sessions/store.session-lifecycle-mutation.test.ts src/config/sessions/artifacts.test.ts src/config/sessions/store.pruning.test.ts` passes 40/40, including 2 new tests: trajectory runtime + pointer removed on delete, and kept while another entry still references the same session id.
- Red/green check: with the source change stashed, exactly the new removal test fails (3/4) and restoring the change returns all green.
- Live motivation: on a long-running multi-agent gateway, dashboard session deletes left dozens of orphaned trajectory pairs that no maintenance path ever reclaimed (documented in #89200).
- Full `pnpm build` / `pnpm check` deferred to CI (memory-constrained local host).

target.title: fix: active-memory recalls from all agents serialize on one shared lane
target.body:
Related: #72015 (this addresses the recall-lane serialization portion of that report; the QMD boot-initialization portion is separate)

> This PR is AI-assisted: the analysis, patch, and test update were written with an AI coding agent. A human operator reviewed the change and validated it against a live deployment.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where, on multi-agent gateways, memory recall runs from different agents queue behind each other. The active-memory recall subagent always enqueues on the single shared `active-memory` lane, and command lanes default to `maxConcurrent: 1`, so every agent's recall serializes globally. The lane wait burns the recall's turn-scoped time budget, so under concurrent traffic (several agents active at once, or a burst of session resets) recalls run late, time out, or are skipped, and users see replies without memory context.

## Why This Change Was Made

Key the recall lane by agent id (`active-memory:<agentId>`) so recalls serialize per agent instead of across the whole gateway. Lanes are created lazily on first use, so no lane registration change is needed. `agentId` is already a required parameter at the enqueue site. Single-agent deployments behave exactly as before (one agent, one lane).

## User Impact

On multi-agent gateways, one agent's memory recall no longer delays every other agent's. Recall latency under concurrent load drops and fewer recall time budgets are exhausted while queued, so memory injection lands more reliably. No configuration change; single-agent installs see no behavioral difference.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-active-memory.config.ts extensions/active-memory/index.test.ts` passes 154/154, including the updated lane assertion (agent `main` now enqueues on `active-memory:main`).
- Live observation motivating the fix: on a multi-agent gateway, recall queue-wait clusters coincided with degraded or skipped memory injection whenever several agents were active in the same window; single-agent sessions on the same build were unaffected.
